title: OFF-HAND · UNILATERAL LEG DAY
vibe: GREEN · THE SWITCH-UP YOU ASKED FOR — no clocks, no 2-mile tempo, no double-bell density. Today is single-side lifting with movements you've never run: cossack, curtsy, kickstand, front-rack lunge. Legs are the work; the treadmill drops to a low-impact walk.
why: You slept 7.5, nothing's sore, and you told me the exercises still feel repetitive. You're right — five of your last six sessions were a KB density/ladder/Tabata block, then a 2-mile treadmill tempo, then a core circuit. Same skeleton, same movement pool: swings, cleans, presses, rows, carries, planks. So today I threw the whole skeleton out. This is a UNILATERAL day: everything single-side, measured by quality reps and controlled tempo instead of a clock, built from the one movement library we've never touched — cossack squats, curtsy lunges, kickstand RDLs, front-rack reverse lunges, single-leg RDLs. Your brain and your hips will feel every one of these because they're new. Two other deliberate switches: (1) it's a LEG day — you haven't done leg strength since 07-18, and loaded single-leg work is the lowest-impact way to hammer your legs, which matters because (2) the 2-mile tempo is OUT. You've run it 5 of 6 sessions — it IS the most repetitive thing you do, and you've now trained four straight days with a tempo each time, so a true impact deload is overdue. Your cardio today is a low-impact incline walk to close, which banks the connective-tissue recovery you're due without a rest day. If you truly can't help yourself, keep the treadmill to an easy 8-10 min — but the single-leg work IS today's leg burn, so let it be.

blocks.title: MOBILITY WARM-UP
blocks.meta: ~7 min · Moves Method Day B (ankles / knees / hips) · prime the single-leg work
blocks.text: Leg day, so we open the hips, ankles and knees and wake up your balance. Original Strength resets: diaphragmatic breathing x5 · rock-backs x10 · cross-crawls 10/side. Then Day B: deep-squat ankle rocks 10/side · toe-squat to heel-squat 8 · 90/90 hip switches 6/side · single-leg balance 20s/side (eyes down, then eyes closed if steady) · leg swings front-back + lateral 10/side · bodyweight cossack squat rehearsal 5/side to open the groin before you load it. Take an extra minute here today — half of these lifts are new to your joints, so grease the pattern before you add weight.

blocks.title: SESSION 1 · UNILATERAL LOWER (the switch-up)
blocks.meta: ~24 min · 50 lb DB / 40 lb bell / 16 kg · single-side · quality reps, no clock
blocks.format: TEMPO HYPERTROPHY · 2 superset pairs, 3 rounds each · RPE 7-8 · 3-sec lowers, pause in the stretch · rest ~60-75s
blocks.workRest: This is NOT a race — there's no timer today on purpose. Move slow and own each rep: 3 seconds down, a real pause at the bottom/stretch, drive up. Do all reps on one side, then switch. If your balance breaks or form gets sloppy, that set's done — quality over count.

items.name: A1 · Kickstand (B-Stance) RDL
items.detail: 50 lb DB · 10/side · working leg flat, back toe just kissing the floor for balance only (~20% of the load). Push hips BACK, feel the hamstring lengthen, pause, drive up. Nearly all the work is on the front leg — a single-leg RDL you can actually load heavy. NEW pattern.

items.name: A2 · Front-Rack Reverse Lunge
items.detail: 40 lb bell in the front rack (one side) · 8/side · step BACK, tall chest, knee to the floor, drive through the front heel. Front-rack loading lights up the quad and forces your midline to stay stacked — a lunge you've never trained this way.

items.name: B1 · Cossack Squat (WILDCARD)
items.detail: 16 kg goblet · 8/side · wide stance, sink into ONE hip keeping the other leg straight, foot flexed. Sit deep, chest up, drive back to center. Brutal on the adductors and hip mobility — a movement you have never done. Go bodyweight the first round if the depth fights you.

items.name: B2 · Single-Leg RDL
items.detail: 16 kg (same-side hand) · 8/side · slight bend in the standing knee, hinge and reach the bell toward the floor, back leg extending behind you like a seesaw. Slow and controlled, feel the hamstring, no rounding. Balance IS the exercise here.

items.name: FINISHER (if time) · Curtsy Lunge
items.detail: 16 kg goblet or bodyweight · 12/side · step the working leg BEHIND and across, hips square, sink and stand. Hits glute med and adductors the straight-line lunges miss. Skip if you're at the 40-min mark.

blocks.text: The whole point of today. Every lift is single-side and every lift is one you don't have grooved, so it'll feel foreign and that's exactly the variety you asked for. Superset A (kickstand RDL + front-rack reverse lunge) is your loaded strength pair — hinge then squat pattern, heavy-ish, 3 rounds. Superset B (cossack + single-leg RDL) is the mobility-strength pair that attacks your frontal plane and your balance, the two things a year of swings and presses never touched. Cossack squat is today's wildcard — nobody trains the sideways plane and yours will be sore in places you forgot you had. No clock anywhere: the discipline today is slow tempo and honest reps, not beating a timer. This is real leg work, so your legs get their burn from strength, not from pounding the treadmill.

blocks.title: SESSION 2 · LOADED ROTATION CORE (your daily core)
blocks.meta: ~8 min · 16 kg / 50 lb DB · fresh midline — no planks, no hollows, no deadbugs
blocks.workRest: 3 unhurried rounds. Different from yesterday's anti-rotation on purpose — today the midline works through loaded bending and rotation, not stillness. Control the weight, don't let it control you.

items.name: Kettlebell Windmill
items.detail: 16 kg overhead (locked out) · 5/side · eyes on the bell, push the same-side hip out, hinge and reach the free hand down your leg toward the floor, stand tall. Loaded lateral flexion + thoracic rotation + hip mobility in one — a core move you haven't done in weeks.

items.name: Half-Kneeling Halo
items.detail: 16 kg · 5 each direction/side · half-kneeling (one knee down), circle the bell tightly around your head. The half-kneel makes your core fight to keep you from tipping while the load orbits — anti-rotation you've never trained. Switch the down-knee each round.

items.name: Suitcase Deadlift-to-Stand + Hold
items.detail: 50 lb DB one side · 6 reps, then a 20s tall hold · deadlift the bell from the floor on ONE side, stand fully, resist getting pulled sideways, then hold tall and don't lean. Anti-lateral-flexion under a real load. Switch sides each round.

blocks.text: Your dedicated daily core block, and I deliberately steered it away from yesterday's anti-rotation planks. Today the midline works dynamically — the windmill bends and rotates you under a locked-out bell (and doubles as hip and shoulder mobility), the half-kneeling halo makes your trunk resist tipping while the weight moves, and the suitcase deadlift-hold trains your obliques to keep you upright against an offset load. All three are single-side, so they ride the same unilateral theme as the leg block. Slow and deliberate — the core adapts to control, not speed.

blocks.title: CARDIO · LOW-IMPACT INCLINE WALK
blocks.meta: ~8 min · treadmill · fat-loss walk, NOT a run — this is the deliberate impact deload
blocks.format: STEADY INCLINE WALK · no intervals, no tempo
blocks.workRest: Set it and walk. Nasal-breathing pace — you should be able to hold a conversation. This is the recovery your legs and connective tissue are due after four straight tempo days.

items.name: Incline Walk
items.detail: 3.0-3.2 mph @ 10-12% incline · ~8 min · tall posture, drive off the toes, don't hold the rails. Burns fat, spikes almost zero joint impact. If you flat-out need to run today, cap it at an EASY 8-10 min Zone 2 (~6 mph / 9:30-10:00 pace) instead — but the honest move is the walk, because the legs already did their work.

blocks.text: Here's the real switch: the 2-mile tempo is out today. You've run it five of your last six sessions — it's the single most repetitive thing you do, and you've now stacked a threshold 2-miler four days running with HR drifting to 90% max. Your engine is a strength, not the problem; cumulative leg IMPACT is the only real risk, and the one thing that's ever deloaded it is backing off the pounding. So today's cardio is a low-impact incline walk that still drives fat loss but gives your knees, hips and Achilles a genuine break, without costing you a full rest day. Own the deload the same way you own the run.

blocks.title: COOLDOWN
blocks.meta: ~3 min · open the hips, groin and hamstrings you just hammered
blocks.text: Walk 60s to settle. Then: deep half-kneeling hip-flexor stretch 30s/side · straddle / frog groin stretch 45s (you loaded the adductors hard with the cossacks) · standing or seated hamstring reach 30s/side · figure-4 glute stretch 30s/side · 5 slow nasal breaths. Report back: which single-leg moves torched you, how the cossacks felt, your RPE, and whether the no-clock / no-tempo format was the variety you wanted — that tells me how far to keep pushing the switch-ups.

timer.emomUnit: NO CLOCK TODAY — Session 1 is tempo reps by feel (3-sec lowers, ~60-75s rest). Use the STOPWATCH only if you want to keep the incline walk honest at ~8 min.
